LC-BUS.ti: 講義“Community Buses in Small Towns”（教師が読み上げる。音声がない場合はスクリプトとして読む）
LC-BUS.c:
In many small towns, bus companies have stopped running some routes because too few people use them. This is a serious problem for older residents who no longer drive. To solve it, some towns now run their own community buses. These are usually small buses that stop near hospitals, supermarkets, and the town office. In one town I visited, the fare is only 100 yen, and the number of riders has risen every year since the service started.
However, community buses are not cheap to operate. The town has to pay for drivers and fuel, and in that town, fares cover only about twenty percent of the cost. Now some towns are trying on-demand buses, which run only when someone books a ride by phone. I think towns should keep looking for new ideas like this, so that everyone can get where they need to go.

LC-FOOD.ti: 講義“Food Loss at Home”（教師が読み上げる。音声がない場合はスクリプトとして読む）
LC-FOOD.c:
Food loss means food that could still be eaten but is thrown away. It happens at every stage, from farms and stores to restaurants and our own homes. In a survey of 300 families in our city, about forty percent of the food thrown away at home had never even been opened.
Why does this happen? One reason is that people buy more than they need, especially when items are on sale. Another reason is confusion about date labels. Many people throw food away as soon as the 'best before' date has passed, even though it is usually still safe to eat for some time after that. There are simple ways to reduce food loss at home. Check your fridge before you go shopping, make a shopping list, and learn what date labels really mean. Small changes in each home can add up to a big difference.

LC-HEAT.ti: 講義“The Urban Heat Island Effect”（教師が読み上げる。音声がない場合はスクリプトとして読む）
LC-HEAT.c:
Have you noticed that the center of a city often feels hotter than the countryside around it? This is called the urban heat island effect, and it has three main causes. First, roads and buildings made of asphalt and concrete absorb heat during the day and release it slowly at night. Second, cities have fewer plants and less open soil. Plants cool the air by releasing water from their leaves, so fewer plants mean less cooling. Third, air conditioners, cars, and factories produce heat.
To reduce the effect, some cities are covering roofs with plants, painting roofs white to reflect sunlight, and planting more trees. These steps cannot remove the problem completely, but together they can make city life more comfortable.

LC-MICR.ti: 講義“Microplastics”（教師が読み上げる。音声がない場合はスクリプトとして読む）
LC-MICR.c:
Have you heard of microplastics? They are pieces of plastic smaller than five millimeters. Some of them are made small on purpose, but many come from larger plastic items. When plastic bottles and bags are left outside, sunlight and waves slowly break them into smaller and smaller pieces. Another source is our clothes. Clothes made of synthetic fibers, such as polyester, can release tiny fibers when they are washed.
These pieces are so small that it is very hard to collect them once they reach the sea, and fish and seabirds sometimes eat them by mistake. So what can we do? The most effective step is to stop plastic from reaching the sea in the first place. We can use fewer single-use plastic products, put our trash in the right place, and join beach clean-ups before large pieces break down.

LC-TREE.ti: 講義“Why Cities Plant Street Trees”（教師が読み上げる。音声がない場合はスクリプトとして読む）
LC-TREE.c:
Today I'd like to talk about street trees. Many cities plant trees along their roads, and there are several good reasons for this. First, trees provide shade. On a hot summer day, the ground under a tree can be much cooler than the ground in the sun. Second, tree roots and soil take in rainwater, so less water runs off the roads after heavy rain. Third, trees give birds and insects places to live, even in the middle of a city. Finally, many people say they feel more relaxed when they walk along a street with trees.
However, street trees also cause some problems. In autumn, fallen leaves must be cleaned up, and large roots can break sidewalks. Taking care of trees also costs money. So when cities plan new streets, they need to choose the right kinds of trees and the right places to plant them.
